purpose: A local Electron cockpit that lets a developer manage Claude Code CLI sessions per-project through a TAB → EPIC → PRD hierarchy, combining terminal, chat, scheduling, and observability into one app.
what: **TAB = project.** A Terminal tab is pinned to one cwd, and everything session-manager tracks for that project lives under `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/` — Epics, scheduler PRDs/queue, the per-project Brief, and `HUMAN_LEARN/` docs — governed by a fail-closed **single-writer law** (`opsOwnership.cjs`) so only the declared owner surface may write each namespace.

**EPIC = one unit of work = one Claude session.** Implemented as `PromptSession`, an Epic mints its own `claudeSessionId`, fixes its title/objective as the first prompt, and offers Chat and Terminal as two views over the same session (never two sessions). `status: 'proposed'` is now the human-approval gate that fully replaced the old `feedback/` intake folder and its skills — an Epic proposal already carries its own session + PRD directory, and pressing **Approve & start** kicks it off.

**Scheduler is a browser over TAB→EPIC→PRD**, not an owner of new state: PRDs live per-project under `scheduler/epics/<epic-id>/prds/` (flat `scheduler/prds/` retired), queue/history shards in `scheduler/state/`, and only a machine-wide session slot pool (`sessionSlots.cjs`, cap ≤3 concurrent `claude -p`) plus run logs remain global. Recent work (through 2026-07-31, v0.39.4/v0.40.3) hardened Epic/Scheduler integration — rollback on failed PRD writes, sourcePromptId provenance, a durable per-Epic prompt/response transcript store, and live-streaming Epic threads.

Beyond the Epics/Scheduler core, the app carries 25+ config/observability tabs (Settings, Skills, Hooks, MCP Servers, Memory Clusters, Web Remote, Permissions, etc.) built on isolated zustand stores fed by IPC broadcasts from the main process, plus a mobile web cockpit at bilko.run (Clerk-authed, same-origin relay, desktop-as-source-of-truth).

scope.text: Single-writer law over session-manager-operations/: every namespace has exactly one owning writer, fail-closed, with a narrow declared-delegation table for cross-writer exceptions.
Persist full prompt/response text to a durable per-Epic transcript store so chat context can be rebuilt from disk.
Epic proposals (status: 'proposed' + Approve & start) fully replaced the feedback/ intake folder, /process-feedback and /my-feedback skills, and the scheduler's 5-minute feedback sweep.
A project's cwd is registered as an allowed write root at createPrd() time to fix epic-scoped PRD writes.
Rollback active-index.json entries when a freshly-minted Epic's PRD write fails, including when the minted-epic dir is non-empty.
Chat/scheduler external-send targets resolve against Epics, not just SessionTabs; scheduler response events broadcast live into open Epic threads.
Scheduler/Plans/Background-Agents consolidated into one Scheduler nav destination after LeftNav grew to ~31 overlapping destinations.
TAB→EPIC→PRD domain model introduced: epic-scoped PRDs, per-project scheduler state, machine-wide session slot pool.

conventions: Tab ID = claudeSessionId; never mint a second session when switching Chat/Terminal views of the same Epic.
All fs writes go through config.cjs's writeJson/writeTextAtomic with an explicit `writer` tag enforced by opsOwnership.cjs — no raw fs writes into session-manager-operations/.
Zustand stores never cross-subscribe (config.ts, live.ts, voice.ts, scheduleState.ts, toast.ts are isolated islands); compose via selectors in components.
Never return a freshly-built value from a zustand selector (`?? []`, `.filter()`, `.map()` inline) — causes React #185 blank-app; select raw slice, derive after. Enforced by `npm run lint:selectors`.
Cap concurrent `claude -p` jobs at 3 machine-wide (scheduler + chatRunner + slot pool) — prior 5x concurrency OOM-killed Electron.
No `shell: true` in child_process.spawn except watchers.cjs and app:test-fire-hook.
New PRDs must mint/join an Epic via scripts/mint-epic.cjs or scheduler_create_prd MCP tool; flat scheduler/prds/ is retired.
Before adding a new LeftNav tab for live/observability data, check whether an existing surface (Terminal, Scheduler) should own it instead of duplicating.
